Saves an EPUB or PDF into the ebook library, in a folder named for `author` and `title`,
adds it to the library, then applies the form's metadata edits and cover. Everything the
server can refuse is checked before the file is saved, so a refused upload leaves nothing
behind. When the file is saved but can't be added as a book, the answer is a 500 whose
body says whether the file was kept. Needs the upload permission.

cover.description:
An image to use as the cover, under 10 MB, with an `image/*` content type. SVG is
refused. Wins over `cover_url`.

cover_url.description:
A metadata provider's cover URL for the server to fetch as the cover. Only the
providers' own `https` hosts are fetched.

overrides.description:
A JSON `MetadataOverrides` object holding the fields you changed from what inspect
returned. Up to 256 KiB.

series_index.description: The book's place in its series, such as `2` or `2.5`.

title.description: The book's title. With `author`, it names the folder the file is saved in.

201.description: The book is in the library.

400.description: A part is missing or invalid, such as no `title` or `author`, a field too long, `overrides` that isn't valid JSON or a refused cover; or no ebook library folder is set up, or it is read-only. The body says which.

403.description: Your account lacks the upload permission.

415.description: The file isn't an EPUB or PDF.

502.description: The server couldn't reach the host of `cover_url`.

post.summary: Inspect an ebook before uploading it
post.description:
Reads the metadata embedded in an EPUB or PDF, so you can review it before sending the
file to `POST /api/uploads/ebooks`. Nothing is saved. Needs the upload permission.

400.description: The form has no `file` part.

403.description: Your account lacks the upload permission.

415.description: The file isn't an EPUB or PDF, or can't be read as one.

get.summary: List the readers whose stats you can see
get.description:
You first, then every other reader who shares their stats, by name. Pass a reader's
`id` as `user_id` to the stats routes to read theirs.

200.description: You, then the readers who share their stats.

get.description:
Any user's profile picture, for drawing beside their name. By default a WebP thumbnail
at most 160 pixels on its longest edge; `size=full` gets the image as uploaded. The URL
stays the same when the user replaces their avatar, so revalidate with `If-None-Match`.

parameters.description:
`full` for the image as uploaded. Anything else, or leaving it out, gets a WebP
thumbnail at most 160 pixels on its longest edge.

304.description: The avatar is unchanged since the `ETag` sent in `If-None-Match`.

404.description: No user has that id, or the user has no avatar.

book_uuids.description: The uuids of the books to add, up to 2000.

AddPhysicalOnlyRequest.description:
A book the library doesn't have, to add as a physical copy only. The server creates a
book with no files and checks in its first copy.

AdminHealthReport.description:
The server health report from `GET /api/admin/health`: the library index, the task
queue, the search index, disk use and recent errors, in one response.

AdminUserRow.description:
A user account in the admin user list, `GET /api/admin/users`. It never carries a
password.

created_at.description: When the account was created, in Unix seconds.

display_name.description: The name other users see. Null when the user hasn't set one.

locked.description:
True while too many wrong passwords keep the account locked.
`POST /api/admin/users/{id}/unlock` unlocks it.

AlignmentAudioFile.description: One of a book's audio files.

chapter_starts.description: Where each chapter in the file starts, in seconds from the start of the file.

label.description: The file's path inside the library folder.

AlignmentAudioPosition.description: Your listening position, as the alignment shows it.

book_file_id.description: The audio file the position is in. Absent when the position didn't name one.

client_updated_at.description: When the device recorded the position, in Unix seconds.

seconds.description: The position, in seconds from the start of the file.

AlignmentEbook.description: The ebook's timeline: its length and where each chapter starts.

total_chars.description: The ebook's length in visible characters.

AlignmentEbookChapter.description: One chapter on the ebook's timeline.

anchor_path.description:
The CFI step path of the chapter's start inside its spine document, such as
`/4/2/6`, when the chapter shares that document with another chapter. It tells a
client which of them a position is in. Absent when the chapter has its spine
document to itself.

percent.description: How far through the book the chapter starts, from 0 to 100.

spine_index.description:
The 0-based spine document the chapter starts in. Match a CFI's spine step against it
to find a position's chapter. The rounded `percent` can land one chapter ahead when
a chapter starts close to the position.

AlignmentLink.description: The link between a book's formats that you confirmed.

confirmed_at.description: When you confirmed the link, in Unix seconds.

follow.description:
Whether follow mode is on. With it on, a client moves to the newer position in the
other format without asking.

primary_book_file_id.description: The narration aligned with the ebook, in `narrations` mode.

stale.description:
Whether the audio files changed since you confirmed the link. Sync is paused until
you confirm it again.

user_anchors.description: How many sync points you declared with `POST /api/books/{uuid}/sync-point`.

AlignmentMatch.description: How well the ebook's chapters matched the audio's, such as 12 of 14 chapter titles.

ebook_chapters.description: How many chapters the ebook has.

matched.description: How many ebook chapters matched an audio chapter.

AlignmentPosition.description: Your reading position, as the alignment shows it.

client_updated_at.description: When the device recorded the position, in Unix seconds.

percent.description:
How far through the book, from 0 to 100. Absent for a moment after a position
arrives with only a CFI, until the server works out the percent.

AlignmentView.description:
How a book's ebook and audiobook line up, as `GET /api/books/{uuid}/alignment` returns
it: the link and whether it is out of date, both formats' timelines, and your position
in each.

oneOf.description:
How well the ebook's chapters matched the audio's. For an unlinked book it shows what
a `sequence` link would get. Absent when nothing anchors the mapping, which then
works by proportion, and when `link.stale` is true.

anchor_pairs.description:
The pairs of points the mapping runs through, in ebook order. Each pair is the
fraction through the ebook, then the fraction through the audio, both from 0 to 1.
Empty when nothing anchors the mapping.

audio_chapter_marks.description:
How many usable chapter marks the audio has. Untitled marks don't count, and neither
do the "Part 1", "Part 2" marks the server makes for files without chapters. When
`anchor_match` is absent, zero means the audio has no chapter marks, and more than
zero means its marks didn't match the ebook. Always zero when `link.stale` is true,
so check that first.

audio_files.description: The book's audio files, in their stored order.

oneOf.description:
The ebook's timeline. Absent when the book has no EPUB, or the server hasn't measured
it yet.
The link you confirmed. Absent when the formats aren't linked.
Your listening position. Absent when you have none.
Your reading position. Absent when you have none.

ApiTokenView.description:
An API token, as `GET /api/auth/api-tokens` lists it. It never carries the secret,
which only `CreateApiTokenResponse` shows.

last_used_at.description:
When the token last authenticated a request, in Unix seconds. Null until its
first use.

suffix.description:
The token's last 4 characters, for showing it as `omni_…xxxx`. Null for tokens
created before Omnibus recorded them.

AttributedRating.description: Another user's rating of a book, with who gave it.

has_avatar.description: Whether the rater has an avatar. `GET /api/users/{user_id}/avatar` serves it.

stars.description: The star rating, from 0.5 to 5 in half-star steps.

updated_at.description: When the rating was last set, in Unix seconds.

username.description: The rater's display name, or their username when they have none.

body_html.description: `body_md` rendered to HTML, with unsafe markup removed.

body_md.description: The public review text, as Markdown. Null for a rating with no text.

created_at.description:
When the review first had stars or text, in Unix seconds. Adding text to a review that
had none restarts it, so a text review dates from its text.

created_at_iso.description: The same moment as `created_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

has_avatar.description: Whether the reviewer has an avatar. `GET /api/users/{user_id}/avatar` serves it.

rated_at.description: When they last changed the stars, in Unix seconds. Null when there are none.

rated_at_iso.description: The same moment as `rated_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

spoiler.description:
Whether the reviewer marked the review as containing spoilers. The stars are never
a spoiler; hide only the text.

stars.description: The star rating, from 0.5 to 5 in half-star steps. Null when they gave none.

updated_at.description: When they last changed the stars, text or spoiler flag, in Unix seconds.

updated_at_iso.description: The same moment as `updated_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

username.description: The reviewer's display name, or their username when they have none.

AudiobookInspection.description:
The metadata `POST /api/uploads/audiobooks/inspect` reads from an uploaded
audiobook's tags.

cover_preview.description:
A small `data:` URL of the first part's cover art, to show before the book exists.
Null when there is none.

creators.description:
Every creator the tags name, starting with `author`. Audio files carry one artist
tag, so the list holds one name at most.

duration_seconds.description:
The combined running time of every part, in seconds. Null when the tags give no
duration.

format.description: The format as a lowercase extension: `m4b`, `m4a` or `mp3`.

has_cover.description: Whether any uploaded part carries embedded cover art.

part_count.description:
How many files the upload holds. It is 1 for an `.m4b` or `.m4a`, and one per part
for an `.mp3` audiobook.

next_file_id.description:
The book's next audio file, by `id`. A player moves on to it when this file
ends, rather than marking the book finished. Null on the last file, and when
the book's files are separate narrations of the whole book.

The book's next audio file, by `id`. A player moves on to it when this file
ends, rather than marking the book finished. Null on the last file, and when
the book's files are separate narrations of the whole book.

AudiobookManifest.description:
How to play one audiobook file, from `GET /api/audiobooks/{uuid}/manifest`. In
`direct` mode each part has a URL to stream with `Range` requests. In `hls` mode one
playlist plays a server-side transcode, for formats a player can't decode. Both modes
carry `book_file_id`, the file a progress write must name, and `audio_file_count`.
When the count is above 1, a position means something only with its file id. A 0 in
either field means the server didn't say.

AudiobookPlaybackRateRecord.description: The playback speed you saved for one audiobook.

updated_at.description: When the speed was saved, in Unix seconds.

AudiobookPlaybackRateUpdate.description: A new playback speed for one audiobook. `playback_rate` runs from 0.5 to 3.0.

AudiobookStatus.description: How far an audiobook's HLS transcode has got, from `GET /api/audiobooks/{uuid}/status`.

progress.description: How far the transcode has got, from 0.0 to 1.0.

ready.description: Whether the transcode has finished. It is an older field, so read `state` instead.

AudiobookStatusState.description:
Where an audiobook's HLS transcode stands: `preparing` while it is queued or running,
`ready` once every segment is made, and `failed` when it failed, which isn't retried on
its own.

AuthorDetail.description: An author and every book by them, from `GET /api/authors/{id}`.

has_photo.description:
Whether the server holds a photo of the author, uploaded or found on Open
Library. When true, `GET /api/authors/{id}/photo` serves it.

reading.description:
Your state on each of `books` that you have opened or marked. A book missing
here is unread, with no position.

AuthorPhotoScanResult.description:
The result of `POST /api/authors/{id}/photo/scan`. `resolved` is false when Open
Library has no photo of the author. Omnibus then stops searching for one by itself.

url.description: An `http` or `https` URL of a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image, up to 2048 bytes.

AuthorReading.description: Your progress through one author's books, from `GET /api/authors/reading`.

finished.description: How many of the author's books you have finished.

last_read_at.description:
The latest `last_read_at` of your `BookReading` across the author's books, in
Unix seconds.

reading.description: How many of the author's books you are reading now.

AuthorSummary.description:
One author in `GET /api/authors`, without their books. `GET /api/authors/{id}`
has the books.

accent.description: The `accent` of the author's first book that has one. Absent when none does.

has_photo.description:
Whether the server holds a photo of the author, as `has_photo` in
`AuthorDetail`.

BackgroundTaskRecord.description:
One recorded run of a background task: its kind, status and timing. Clients can read
these but never write them.

error.description:
Why the run failed. Null unless `status` is `failed`. The text is safe to show
and holds no server internals.

finished_at.description: When the run finished, in Unix seconds. Null while `status` is `running`.

started_at.description: When the run started, in Unix seconds.

BackgroundTaskStatus.description:
Where a recorded background task run ended up. `running` also covers a run that never
finished because the server stopped abruptly.

BookDeletionImpact.description: The reader data that deleting a book removes, counted across every reader.

shelves.description: How many hand-picked shelves hold the book.

BookDeletionManifest.description:
What an admin can delete for one book: its files and physical copies, and the reader
data that deleting all of them would take with the book.

BookFileInfo.description: One of a book's files on disk. A book can have several, such as two EPUB editions.

duration_seconds.description:
The file's playing time in whole seconds, summed over its parts. Present for audio
files only.

etag.description:
The file's content validator. Save it with a download and compare it with a later
value. A different value means the downloaded copy is stale. Absent until the
server has read the file's size and modification time. A missing value on either
side means you can't tell, not that the copy is current.

path.description:
The file's path inside the library folder, such as `clarke/piranesi.epub`. Absent
for a few files indexed by old versions of Omnibus.

BookHouseholdReader.description:
A reader who shares their stats and has spent time in one book, as
`GET /api/books/{uuid}/household` lists them.

has_avatar.description: Whether `GET /api/users/{id}/avatar` has an image to serve.

id.description: The user's id. Pass it as `user_id` to the stats routes.

last_session_at.description: When their latest sitting of a minute or more ended, in Unix seconds.

name.description: The reader's display name, or their username when they have none.

seconds.description: Seconds they have read and listened in the book, short glances included.

sessions.description: How many times they sat down with it for a minute or more.

BookImage.description: One image in an EPUB's manifest.

byte_size.description: The image's uncompressed size in bytes.

href.description:
The image's path inside the EPUB. `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/images/file` and
`GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/images/link` take it as `href`.

media_type.description: The media type the manifest declares, such as `image/png`.

references.description: Each spine document that shows the image, in spine order. Empty when none does.

width.description:
The width in pixels. Null when the image header can't be read, which includes
every SVG.

BookImageLink.description:
A link that fetches one image's original bytes without signing in. `path` is a
server-relative `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/images/signed` path that opens that one image
only. It works until `expires_at`, in Unix seconds.

BookImageList.description: Every image the manifest of a book's EPUB lists, from `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/images`.

BookImageReference.description: One spine document that shows an image.

alt.description:
The image's alt text where the document first shows it. Null when there is none,
and always for an SVG image.

spine_index.description: The document's spine index, as in `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters`.

BookInsights.description: One user's reading and listening in one book.

as_of_day.description: Today, as `YYYY-MM-DD` in your time zone. It is the last day `daily` could cover.

daily.description:
Seconds per day in the book, active days only, oldest first. Days are in your time
zone. Fill the gaps up to `as_of_day`.

longest_started_at.description: When the longest sitting started, in Unix seconds.

seconds_total.description:
Seconds read and listened in the book, including sittings too short to count in
`sessions`.

sessions.description:
How many sittings the book had, which is how often it was picked up. A sitting is
recorded time on the book with no break over 15 minutes, in either format. Sittings
under a minute don't count.

sitting_seconds.description:
Seconds in the sittings `sessions` counts. Divide it by `sessions` for the mean
sitting, which `seconds_total` would skew. Never more than `seconds_total`.

started_at.description: When the first session in the book started, in Unix seconds.

BookProgress.description:
Every position you have in one book, one per format, as `GET /api/progress/{uuid}`
returns it. The `format` query parameter narrows `records` to one entry.

book_uuid.description:
The uuid of the book the positions belong to. It differs from the uuid in the path
when that book was merged into this one.

oneOf.description:
Where to resume in the other format, for a linked book. It is mapped from your
position in `furthest`. Absent when there is nothing newer to offer or the position
can't be mapped.

The format of the record that is your true place. It is the record furthest through
the book by whole-book percent, or the most recent when a record has no percent.
Null only when `records` is empty.

linked.description:
Whether you have linked this book's ebook and audiobook, so positions sync between
them.

records.description:
One record per format you have a position in, the most recently recorded first.
Empty when you have never opened the book.

BookReading.description:
Your state on one book: its status, how far in you are, and when you last read it.
A book with a position but no status set reads as `reading`.

book_file_id.description:
The audio file of your latest position, by its `id` in the book's `book_files`.
Absent without one.

oneOf.description:
The format of your latest position, so a client resumes in the same reader or
player. Absent without a position.

last_read_at.description:
When you last read the book, in Unix seconds. It is the time your device gave the
latest position, or else the time the status changed. Absent for a book marked
`unread`.

percent.description:
Your latest position as a whole-book percent, rounded down. Absent without a
position.

BookRef.description: The uuid of the book a check-in, physical-only add or wishlist add wrote to.

BookReviews.description: Everything readers have said about one book.

oneOf.description: Your own review. Null when you haven't reviewed the book.

others.description:
Other readers' reviews: those with text first, newest first by when the text was
first written, then ratings with no text, most recently rated first. A review
holding only private notes isn't listed.

oneOf.description: The book's ratings summed up. Null until at least two readers have rated it.

BookSuggestion.description:
A book Hardcover suggests for readers of a library book. It is not in the library;
`hardcover_url` links to it on Hardcover.

cover_url.description:
The path of the cached cover, `/api/suggestions/{uuid}/{rank}/cover`, relative to
the server. Null when no cover is cached.

list_count.description:
How many curated Hardcover lists hold both this book and the one it was
suggested for. A higher count means a stronger match.

BookSuperlative.description: A book that holds one of the period's records, and the figure it holds it with.

author.description: The book's first author. Null when it has none.

value.description:
The figure. Its unit depends on the `Superlatives` field that holds it: pages,
seconds or days.

Bookmark.description: A saved place in a book, in an ebook or an audiobook.

chapter_title.description:
The title of the chapter the bookmark is in, from the book's table of contents.
Null when the server doesn't know the book's chapters.

client_id.description:
The id the creating device gave the bookmark. Null when the device sent none, and
for bookmarks made by old versions of Omnibus.

created_at.description: When the bookmark was made, in Unix seconds.

created_at_iso.description: The same moment as `created_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

percent_through_book.description:
How far through the book the bookmark is, from 0 to 100. It measures to the start of
the spine document the bookmark is in, not to the bookmark itself.

position.description:
Where the bookmark is: an EPUB CFI in an ebook, or a number of seconds as a decimal
string in an audiobook. The server stores it as the client sent it.

spine_index.description:
The 0-based index of the spine document the bookmark is in, as
`GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters` numbers them. Null for an audiobook bookmark, one
made on a Kobo, and any position the server can't read.

title.description: The bookmark's name or note. Null when it has none.

BulkMetadataEdit.description:
One edit applied to many books at once. A text field that is absent leaves every
book's value as it is, and a value sets it on every book. An empty string is
reserved. `authors` replaces each book's whole list of creators. The tag and genre
fields add to or remove from each book's own list.

BulkOverridesRequest.description: The body of the bulk metadata edit: the books to change and the edit to apply to each.

uuids.description: The uuids of the books to edit.

CapturedError.description: One error the server logged recently. The server keeps the last 200.

book_uuid.description: The uuid of the book the error names. Absent when it names none.

file.description: The file path the error names. Absent when it names none.

message.description: The error message, or an empty string when there is none.

target.description: The part of the server code that logged the error.

timestamp.description: When the error was logged, in Unix seconds.

current_password.description: Your password now, to prove it is you.

new_password.description: The password to switch to. It must meet the same rules as at sign-up.

ChapterInfo.description: A chapter on an audiobook file's timeline.

ChapterListEntry.description: One entry of a book's table of contents, with the spine index its text is read by.

ordinal.description: The entry's place in the table of contents, counted from 0.

spine_index.description:
The spine document the entry points to. Pass it to
`GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters/{spine_index}/text`.

ChapterListResponse.description:
A book's table of contents, from `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters`. `has_text` is
false when the book has no text to read, such as a comic or an audiobook. An EPUB
without a table of contents has `has_text` true and an empty `chapters`. Its text can
still be read by spine index.

spine_count.description:
The number of spine documents. Text can be read at spine indexes from 0 to one
less than this. 0 when `has_text` is false.

ChapterTextResponse.description:
One slice of a spine document's text as plain prose, from
`GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters/{spine_index}/text`. A slice holds up to 100,000
characters. When `has_text` is false, the book has no text and the other fields are
empty or 0.

next_offset.description: The `offset` to request for the next slice. Null when the slice reaches the end.

offset.description:
Where the slice starts, in characters from the start of the document. It echoes
the request's `offset`.

total_chars.description: The length of the whole document's text, in characters.

truncated.description: Whether the document goes on past this slice.

truncated_by_progress.description:
Whether the slice stops at your furthest reading position, as `stop_at_progress`
asks. `truncated` is then false and `next_offset` null, since there is nothing to
continue to. Absent when false.

ChartAxis.description: One axis of the rendered chart.

max.description:
Upper bound of the axis. Always > 0 — a flat-zero axis is nudged to 1
so the renderer never divides by zero.

ChartBreakdown.description: An optional split of a single measure into several series.

ChartBucket.description:
How wide each bucket on the x-axis is: a day, a week (starting Monday), a month or a
year. The x-axis is always time.

ChartMark.description:
How a series is drawn. Derived from the measure, never picked by the
reader — a pie chart of minutes-over-time is a question the builder should
not be able to ask.

ChartMeasure.description:
What a chart can plot: one number per bucket, in a unit of its own. Measures sharing a
unit share a scale, and a chart holds at most two scales.

ChartResult.description: The series a chart spec asks for, aligned on one shared set of buckets.

axes.description: Left axis, then optionally the right.

bucket.description:
The granularity `buckets` are keyed at. Carried on the answer so a
renderer can label the axis without being handed the spec separately —
and so a result can never be labelled at a granularity it wasn't
bucketed at.

buckets.description:
The shared x-axis: bucket keys ascending. `YYYY-MM-DD` for Day and
Week (the week's Monday), `YYYY-MM` for Month, `YYYY` for Year.

caveats.description: Caveats carried by the selected measures.

divisions.description:
Gridlines dividing the plot, shared by both axes. Two different counts
would put the right axis's labels between the lines they belong to.

stacked.description:
Whether the bar series stack into one column per bucket.

Only true for a **breakdown of one additive measure**, where the slices are
parts of a whole. Different measures never stack, nor does a split average,
since means do not add.

truncated.description: Set when `buckets` was clipped to the most recent 366.

ChartSeries.description:
One plotted series: a measure (optionally narrowed to a breakdown slice) and
its value in every bucket of the shared axis. `values` is positionally
aligned with `buckets`; null means *no data*, which for an average is a real
state and not a zero.

axis.description: Which axis this series is scaled against — `0` left, `1` right.

slice.description: The breakdown slice this series describes, when the spec asked for one.

ChartSpec.description: What a reader composed in the builder.

breakdown.description:
Optional split. Allowed only with exactly one measure, and only one that
supports a split (a per-book measure); any other combination is rejected.

measures.description:
The measures to plot, each at most once. Measures that share a unit share a
scale, and a second unit opens the right-hand axis. A third unit is rejected.

range.description: The window, reusing the stats page's own range vocabulary.

ChartUnit.description:
The unit a measure is expressed in. Two measures sharing a unit share an
axis; a second distinct unit opens the right-hand axis.

CheckInRequest.description:
A physical copy to check in, of a book the library already has. `isbn` may be up to
32 characters and `note` up to 4096.

CleanupAction.description: What a cleanup suggestion proposes doing.

CleanupCounts.description: How many cleanup suggestions are in each review state.

log_id.description:
The change an accept applied, which `POST /api/admin/cleanup/undo/{log_id}` reverses.
Null for a reject, which changes nothing.

CleanupDecisionRequest.description: A reviewer's decision on one cleanup suggestion.

decision.description: `accepted` applies the suggestion and `rejected` dismisses it. `pending` is refused.

value.description:
The reviewer's own wording, used in place of the proposed one. Only a book-title
rename takes it; for any other suggestion it is refused.

CleanupKind.description: What a cleanup suggestion is about: an author, a series, a tag or a book's title.

CleanupKindCounts.description: One kind's suggestions counted by review state.

counts.description: How many of that kind's suggestions are in each review state.

kind.description: The kind of record the suggestions are about.

allOf.description: A new bookmark, as `POST /api/bookmarks` takes it.

client_id.description:
An id the device makes up for the bookmark, such as a UUID, up to 64 characters. The
`/api/bookmarks/{id}` routes accept it in place of `id`, so an offline client can
use the bookmark before the server has numbered it. Sending the same `client_id`
again returns the bookmark already stored instead of making a second one.

position.description:
Where the bookmark is: an EPUB CFI in an ebook, or a number of seconds as a decimal
string in an audiobook. Up to 4,096 characters.

title.description: The bookmark's name or note, up to 512 characters.

client_created_at.description:
When the device made the item, in Unix seconds. The server uses its own clock when
this is absent or in the future.

ClientStamped_CreateBookmark.description:
A create body plus the time the device made the item: the wrapped body's fields and
`client_created_at`, side by side in one JSON object. Highlight, bookmark and journal
creates take this shape, so an offline client that sends a create later keeps the time
of the gesture.

allOf.description: A new highlight, as `POST /api/highlights` takes it.

client_id.description:
An id the device makes up for the highlight, such as a UUID, up to 64 characters. The
`/api/highlights/{id}` routes accept it in place of `id`, so an offline client can
use the highlight before the server has numbered it. Sending the same `client_id`
again returns the highlight already stored instead of making a second one.

epub_cfi_range.description: The highlighted range, as an EPUB range CFI, up to 4,096 characters.

text.description: The highlighted text, up to 8,192 characters. May be left out.

client_created_at.description:
When the device made the item, in Unix seconds. The server uses its own clock when
this is absent or in the future.

ClientStamped_CreateHighlight.description:
A create body plus the time the device made the item: the wrapped body's fields and
`client_created_at`, side by side in one JSON object. Highlight, bookmark and journal
creates take this shape, so an offline client that sends a create later keeps the time
of the gesture.

allOf.description: A new journal entry, as `POST /api/journals` takes it.

body_md.description: The entry's Markdown source. It must not be blank, and can be up to 65,536 bytes.

client_id.description:
An id the device makes up for the entry, such as a UUID, up to 64 characters. The
`/api/journals/{id}` routes accept it in place of `id`, so an offline client can
edit or delete the entry before the server has numbered it. Sending the same
`client_id` again returns the entry already stored instead of making a second one.

progress.description: How far through the book you are, from 0 to 100. May be null.

status.description: May be left out, which publishes the entry.

client_created_at.description:
When the device made the item, in Unix seconds. The server uses its own clock when
this is absent or in the future.

ClientStamped_CreateJournalEntry.description:
A create body plus the time the device made the item: the wrapped body's fields and
`client_created_at`, side by side in one JSON object. Highlight, bookmark and journal
creates take this shape, so an offline client that sends a create later keeps the time
of the gesture.

CompositionDimension.description:
One way of dividing up the library, such as by format: its buckets and the coverage
behind them. `coverage.total` is the sum of every bucket's `books`, and
`coverage.books` is how many different books the dimension describes. The two differ
when a book falls in more than one bucket. Zero `coverage.books` means no book has
this property.

CompositionSlice.description: One bucket of a `LibraryComposition` dimension: a label and how many books are in it.

ConfirmCrossFormatLink.description:
How a book's ebook and audiobook line up, as `POST /api/books/{uuid}/cross-format-link`
takes it.

audio_order.description:
A new order for the book's audio files, as a list of every `book_file_id` once. It
changes the order for every user, so it needs the edit permission. May be left out.

book_uuid.description: Required, but the server uses the uuid in the path instead.

primary_book_file_id.description: The narration to align with the ebook. Required in `narrations` mode.

ContentSearchHit.description: One chapter that matches a content search, with an excerpt around the match.

ahead_of_reader.description:
Whether the hit is past your furthest recorded position in the book. Absent
under `spoiler_filter=none`, when you have no position in the book, or when the
hit can't be placed in it. Absent does not mean the hit is safe to show.

chapter_title.description:
The chapter's title from the book's table of contents. Absent when Omnibus
hasn't read the book's table of contents.

position_delta_percent.description:
How far the hit is from your position, in whole-book percentage points. A
positive value is ahead of you and a negative one behind. Absent whenever
`ahead_of_reader` is.

snippet.description:
An excerpt around the match. Each matched word is wrapped in `[` and `]`, and
cut text is marked with `…`.

spine_index.description: The spine index of the chapter the match is in, counted from 0.

title.description: The book's title, or its path in the library folder when it has none.

ContentSearchResults.description: The chapters `GET /api/search/content` found, best match first.

hint.description:
Why the result is empty, when the query's wording is the likely cause. A chapter
must hold every word of the query, so a question written as a sentence often
matches nothing while its words alone match plenty. Absent otherwise.

withheld_ahead.description:
How many hits past your position `spoiler_filter=exclude` left out. Always
present under `exclude`, as 0 when it left none out. Absent under the other
modes.

Contributor.description: A person credited on a book, such as an author, an illustrator or a translator.

file_as.description: The name to sort by, such as `Herbert, Frank`. Null when the book doesn't say.

id.description:
The author's id, as in `GET /api/authors/{id}`. Absent when no author in the
library has this name.

role.description:
The person's role as a MARC relator code, such as `aut` for an author or `trl`
for a translator. Null when the book doesn't say.

CoverFromUrlBody.description: The image URL `POST /api/ebooks/{uuid}/cover/from-url` fetches as the book's cover.

url.description:
The image to fetch, up to 2,048 bytes long. Only `https` URLs on public addresses
are fetched.

CreateApiTokenRequest.description: A name for a new API token, 1 to 100 characters.

CreateApiTokenResponse.description:
A new API token. `secret` is the raw `omni_…` token, and this is the only response
that shows it. The server keeps only a hash, so a lost secret can't be recovered.
