edit or delete the entry before the server has numbered it. Sending the same
`client_id` again returns the entry already stored instead of making a second one.

progress.description: How far through the book you are, from 0 to 100. May be null.

status.description: May be left out, which publishes the entry.

CreateKoboDevice.description: The label and kind for a new device.

kind.description: Which kind of device to register. Defaults to a Kobo when omitted.

name.description: A label of 1 to 100 characters once trimmed, such as "Clara HD".

CreateShelfRequest.description:
A new shelf. A `smart` shelf needs `match_mode` and at least one rule, and takes no
`book_uuids`. A `manual` shelf takes no `match_mode` or rules, and may start with
`book_uuids`. A `wishlist` shelf can't be created. `name` is 1 to 120 characters and
`description` at most 2048.

CreateUserRequest.description: A new account for `POST /api/admin/users` to create.

CrossFormatCandidate.description:
Your position in one format, mapped onto the other. The audio fields are set when
`target` is `audio`, and `percent`, `fraction` and `epub_cfi` when it is `epub`.

audio_position_seconds.description: Where to start, in seconds from the start of `book_file_id`.

epub_cfi.description:
The mapped place as a point EPUB CFI. Present only when the request asked for it
with `derive=cfi` and the server could work it out. Otherwise use `fraction`.

fraction.description:
How far through the book, from 0 to 1, at full precision. Jump to this, and show
`percent`.

percent.description: How far through the book, from 0 to 100, rounded down from `fraction`.

source_ahead.description:
Whether the mapped position is ahead of your current position in `target`. False
means the offer moves you back, so don't describe it as further on. Absent when
there is no comparable position in `target`. Treat that as ahead.

source_client_updated_at.description:
The `client_updated_at` of the position it was mapped from, in Unix seconds. A
client can compare it with positions it already knows to avoid offering the same
one twice.

source_format.description: The format the position was mapped from.

source_position_seconds.description:
The listening position it was mapped from, in seconds from the start of the whole
audiobook. Set when `target` is `epub`.

total_duration_seconds.description: The length of the whole audiobook in seconds, across all its files.

CrossFormatLinkMode.description:
How a book's audio files relate to each other. The user says which when linking the
formats; the server never guesses.

CrossFormatResume.description:
Where to resume a book in the other format, as
`GET /api/books/{uuid}/cross-format-resume` returns it.

oneOf.description: The mapped position. Present when `state` is `candidate` or `aligned`.

follow.description:
Whether follow mode is on. With it on, a client moves to a `candidate` position
without asking.

CrossFormatResumeState.description: Whether there is a position to resume in the other format, and if not, why not.

DailyGoal.description:
A reader's daily goal of one kind, with today's progress toward it. Today is in the
time zone of the request's `utc_offset_minutes`, else of the reader's latest session,
else UTC.

current.description: Progress toward `target` on `day`. It can be more than `target`.

kind.description: What the goal counts: `pages` or `minutes`. Minutes count reading and listening.

target.description:
The number to reach each day. At least 1. A cleared goal is null, never a zero
target.

DailyGoalUpdate.description: The daily goal `PUT /api/stats/goal/daily` sets or clears.

target.description:
The number to reach each day: 1 to 2,000 pages, or 1 to 1,440 minutes. Null or
absent clears the goal.

DailyGoals.description:
A reader's daily goals, at most one of each kind. Each is separate from the other and
from the yearly `ReadingGoal`.

oneOf.description: The minutes goal. Null when none is set.

minutes_today.description:
Minutes read and listened today, whether or not a minutes goal is set, over the same
day as `pages_today`. Rounded down, so 59 seconds is not yet a minute.

oneOf.description: The pages goal. Null when none is set.

pages_today.description:
Pages read today, whether or not a pages goal is set. It is the same figure as the
pages goal's `current`, so setting a goal never changes it. Null only when the
server couldn't measure it, never in place of zero.

unzoned_seconds.description: Always 0. Kept so clients built against an older response still decode it.

DayActivity.description: The seconds read and listened on one day.

day.description: The day, as `YYYY-MM-DD` in your time zone.

Decision.description: Where a cleanup suggestion stands in review.

DeclareSyncPoint.description:
A sync point, as `POST /api/books/{uuid}/sync-point` takes it: your position in the
format you're using, which the server pairs with your saved position in the other.

audio_book_file_id.description: The audio file you're playing, for `audio`.

audio_seconds.description:
Your position in seconds from the start of `audio_book_file_id`. Required for
`audio`, and must not be negative.

book_uuid.description: Required, but the server uses the uuid in the path instead.

ebook_fraction.description: How far through the book you are, from 0 to 1. Required for `epub`.

epub_cfi.description:
Your position as an EPUB CFI, for `epub`. May be left out. When present, the server
works out the fraction from it and ignores `ebook_fraction`.

DeleteBookFilesRequest.description:
The files and physical copies `POST /api/books/{uuid}/delete-files` deletes, by `id`.
Either list may be empty or left out. The book itself goes once no file or copy is
left, so two empty lists delete a book that has neither.

book_deleted.description:
True when the book itself was deleted because nothing of it was left. Its uuid
no longer resolves.

DeviceKind.description:
Which kind of reader a registered device is. A token only authenticates the routes of
its own kind.

DeviceView.description:
A registered device, as its owner or an admin sees it.
`GET /api/admin/users/{id}/devices` lists them.

DownloadFormat.description:
Which of a book's two downloads a validator question is about: `epub` for its EPUB,
CBZ or PDF file, and `audio` for its M4B, M4A or MP3 file.

DownloadValidator.description:
The current validator of one file in the request. `etag` is absent when the book, the
format or the file is gone, or when the server has not read the file yet. Read absent
as "can't tell", never as "unchanged".

DownloadValidatorQuery.description: One downloaded file to look up the current validator of.

file_id.description:
The file the download came from, by its `id` in the book's `book_files`, when the
download named one. Leave it out otherwise, and the server answers about the file
it picks by default.

DownloadValidatorRequest.description: The files `POST /api/downloads/validators` looks up, up to 500.

DownloadValidatorResponse.description:
The current validators `POST /api/downloads/validators` found, one per file asked
about.

EbookConvertStatus.description:
Whether the server can run Calibre's `ebook-convert` to convert book formats.
Calibre is optional. Without it, format conversion is off and nothing else is wrong.

path.description:
The command the server runs: a saved path, the `OMNIBUS_EBOOK_CONVERT_PATH`
environment variable, or plain `ebook-convert` found on the server's `PATH`.

The path of Calibre's `ebook-convert`, up to 4096 bytes. Null or blank clears the
saved path.

EbookLibrary.description:
A list of books, either the whole library from `GET /api/ebooks` or the matches from
`GET /api/search`.

total.description:
How many books matched before the list was cut to 50,000. Always null from the
`/api/*` routes, which send that count in the `X-Total-Count` header.

EbookMetadata.description: A book in the library, with any metadata edits applied.

accent.description:
A color picked from the cover, as a CSS color in the form `oklch(L C H)`. Absent
when the book has no cover or no color could be picked.

added_at.description:
When the book was added to the library, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp such as
`2024-05-01T12:00:00Z`. The `newest_added` sort orders by it.

book_files.description:
Every file of the book on disk, including the only file of a single-file book.
Count files per format from this list. Each file's `etag` tells whether a
downloaded copy is stale. Absent in list responses such as `GET /api/ebooks`, and
for a book with no file.

cover_url.description:
The cover's path on this server, `/api/covers/{uuid}`, to join with the server's
base URL. Null when the book has no cover.

creators.description:
The people credited on the book, with the file's creators first and its other
contributors after them.

description.description:
The book's description as sanitized HTML. Null in a `GET /api/ebooks` page
requested with `omit_description=true`, and in its stacks. There, null does not
mean empty. Read the book from `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}` for it.

epub_size_bytes.description:
The size in bytes of the file Send to Kindle emails, which is the book's first
EPUB or else its PDF. Omnibus won't email a file over 50,000,000 bytes. Absent when the
book has neither, and in list responses such as `GET /api/ebooks`.

genres.description:
Genres users have given the book. Book files carry no genre, so this list holds
only what users set.

has_cover_override.description:
Whether `cover_url` serves an uploaded cover rather than the one from the book's
file.

has_override.description:
Whether the book has metadata edits. `DELETE /api/ebooks/{uuid}/overrides`
removes them.

has_physical.description: Whether at least one physical copy of the book is checked in. Absent when false.

isbn10.description:
The book's ISBN-10. Only an edit sets it, since book files don't carry a separate
ISBN-10.

isbn13.description:
The book's ISBN-13. It is an edit's value, or else the first of `identifiers`
whose scheme names ISBN and whose value reads as 13 digits. Absent when there is
none.

last_interacted_at.description:
The last time anyone rated the book, published a journal entry on it, changed its
read status, added it, edited its metadata or cover, or checked in a physical
copy. It is an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp such as `2024-05-01T12:00:00Z`, so it sorts
as text. The `recently_interacted` sort orders by it. Absent only for a book with
none of these events.

page_count.description:
The number of pages in the book's CBZ comic, as
`GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/pages/{page}` serves them. Absent for a book with no CBZ,
an archive that can't be read, or a file Omnibus hasn't counted yet.

print_pages.description:
The page count of a print edition, as a user entered it. It is not `page_count`,
which counts the images in a CBZ comic, and both can be set.

series_id.description:
The series' id, as in `GET /api/series/{id}`. Absent when the book is in no
series.

unique_identifier.description:
The book's uuid, which the `{uuid}` routes take, such as
`GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}`.

stacks.description:
The series folded into one row each. Absent unless the request set `stack_series`
and the page held a series of two or more books.

EbookPage.description:
One response of `GET /api/ebooks`, holding a page of books and the series it folded
into stacks when the request set `stack_series`.

EditionHydrateRequest.description:
One edition to fetch in full from its provider, for
`POST /api/metadata/editions/hydrate`. Send `source` and `provider_ref` exactly as
the edition search returned them. `provider_ref` may be up to 256 bytes.

isbn13.description:
The edition's ISBN-13, when it has one. The server prefers it to `provider_ref`,
because an ISBN names one printing where a handle may name a whole work.

EditionSearchRequest.description:
An edition search across the metadata providers, for
`POST /api/metadata/editions/search`. At least one of `query`, `title`, `author` or
`isbn` must hold text.

author.description: The book's main author, up to 200 characters, to go with `title`.

isbn.description:
An ISBN the client already has for the book, in any format, up to 32 characters.
The server normalizes it and ignores an invalid one. It is the strongest match
signal a search can carry.

providers.description:
The providers to ask. When it is left out, the server asks every configured
provider. An empty list is refused.

query.description: The search as free text, up to 200 characters. A client may send only this.

title.description:
The book's title on its own, up to 200 characters, when the client can separate
it from the author. Each provider then gets the title and author in the fields it
expects. When it is left out, the server treats `query` as the title, with no
author.

EditionSearchResponse.description:
The results of an edition search: every edition the providers returned, and one
status per provider considered, including any the server skipped and any that
failed.

ExternalBookMeta.description:
Book metadata from an external provider. Only `isbn13`, `title` and `source` are
always set, and providers differ on the rest. `cover_url` points at the provider's
image, which the server downloads only when it creates a book or wishlist entry from
this metadata.

first_publish_year.description:
The year the work was first published, in any edition. `year` is this edition's
own date.

isbn13.description: The ISBN-13 that matched, as 13 digits with no hyphens.

series.description:
The series statement, as free text in the provider's own form, such as
"The Kingkiller Chronicle (1)".

year.description: The publication year or date, as free text in the provider's own form.

FetchSummaryBody.description: The provider `POST /api/ebooks/{uuid}/summary/fetch` asks for a summary.

FileBytes.description:
A file's raw bytes, such as an image, an EPUB or an audio part. It is never JSON. The
operation's content type says what the bytes are.

FinishedBook.description:
A book finished in the period. A book counts as finished when its read status is set
to `finished`, or a journal entry on it says 100 percent.

author.description: The book's first author. Null when it has none.

cover_url.description: `/api/covers/{uuid}` when the book has a cover. Null when it has none.

finished_at.description:
When the book was finished, in Unix seconds. The latest time, if it was finished
more than once.

finished_at_iso.description: The same moment as `finished_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

rating.description:
The reader's star rating of the book, from 0.5 to 5. Null when they haven't rated
it.

FtsHealth.description:
Whether the search index lists every book. A mismatch means an earlier write failed
to update the index. `POST /api/fts/rebuild` brings it back in sync.

GenreShare.description:
A genre and how many books with it were read or listened to in the period. It counts
books, not seconds.

GenreWeight.description: A genre and the number of books that carry it.

GhostFilesWarning.description:
How many books lost their files in one scan. `removed` books lost theirs, out of the
`total` that had files. The share was high enough to warn about, but below the point
where the scan stops.

GoogleBooksKeyStatus.description:
Whether the server has a Google Books API key, with the key masked. It never carries
the key itself.

masked.description: A masked preview of the key, such as `AIza…9f3a`. Null when no key is set.

source.description:
Where the key in effect comes from: `settings` when saved through the API, `env`
when read from the server's environment variables, or `none`.

HardcoverKeyStatus.description:
Whether the server has a Hardcover API key, with the key masked. It never carries the
key itself.

masked.description: A masked preview of the key, such as `hc_l…3f9a`. Null when no key is set.

source.description:
Where the key in effect comes from: `settings` when saved through the API, `env`
when read from the server's environment variables, or `none`.

Health.description: A running server's liveness and build details.

app.description: Always `omnibus`, which tells this server apart from another program on the port.

build_id.description:
When this server process started, in Unix milliseconds. It changes on every restart,
so a new value means a rebuilt server is up.

repo_root.description:
The directory the server runs from. Development tooling uses it to tell the servers of
two checkouts apart.

time.description: The server's clock in Unix seconds, so a client can measure how far its own clock is off.

version.description: The release, such as `v0.9.3`, or `dev` for a local build.

Highlight.description: A highlighted passage in an ebook, with an optional note.

chapter_title.description:
The title of the chapter the highlight is in, from the book's table of contents.
Null when the server doesn't know the book's chapters.

client_id.description:
The id the creating device gave the highlight. Null when the device sent none, and
for highlights made by old versions of Omnibus.

created_at.description: When the highlight was made, in Unix seconds.

created_at_iso.description: The same moment as `created_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

epub_cfi_range.description:
The highlighted range, as an EPUB range CFI. For a highlight made on a Kobo, the
server works it out from the Kobo's own location. Null while that fails. A client
can list such a highlight but can't place it in the text.

note.description: The note on the highlight. Null when it has none.

percent_through_book.description:
How far through the book the highlight is, from 0 to 100. It measures to the start of
the spine document the highlight is in, not to the highlight itself.

spine_index.description:
The 0-based index of the spine document the highlight is in, as
`GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters` numbers them. Null when the highlight has no
`epub_cfi_range` or the server can't read it.

text.description: The highlighted text. Null for a few highlights made by old versions of Omnibus.

HighlightColor.description: A highlight's color, one of five.

HourBucket.description: One hour of the day and the seconds read and listened in it during the period.

hour.description:
The hour, from 0 to 23, on the clock where each session happened. The server reads
it from the UTC offset the session recorded, not from your time zone.

HouseholdReader.description: A reader on this server, as `GET /api/users` lists them.

has_avatar.description: Whether `GET /api/users/{id}/avatar` has an image to serve.

id.description: The user's id. Pass it as `user_id` to the stats routes.

is_you.description: True for the signed-in user, who always comes first.

name.description: The reader's display name, or their username when they have none.

Identifier.description:
An identifier the book's file declares, such as an ISBN:
`{"scheme": "ISBN", "value": "9780441013593"}`.

IndexStatus.description:
What the library index holds: the configured library folders and how many books,
authors and series it lists.

ghosted_book_count.description:
Books that have lost every file because a scan no longer found them on disk. The
book records stay.

JournalEntry.description: A Markdown note a user wrote about a book.

author_has_avatar.description: Whether the author has an avatar. `GET /api/users/{user_id}/avatar` serves it.

author_id.description: The id of the user who wrote the entry.

author_name.description: The author's display name, or their username when they have none.

body_html.description: The entry rendered to HTML, with unsafe markup removed.

body_md.description: The entry's Markdown source, for editing.

client_id.description:
The id the creating device gave the entry. Null when the device sent none, and for
entries written with old versions of Omnibus.

created_at.description: When the entry was written, in Unix seconds.

created_at_iso.description: The same moment as `created_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

progress.description:
How far through the book the author was, from 0 to 100. Null when they didn't say.
An entry at 100 counts the book as finished in the author's reading stats.

updated_at.description: When the entry was last edited, in Unix seconds.

updated_at_iso.description: The same moment as `updated_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

url.description: The image's URL. Put it in an entry's Markdown as `![caption](url)`.

JournalStatus.description:
Who can see a journal entry. A draft is visible only to its author. A published entry,
the default, is visible to every user.

KindleDelivery.description:
Whether Send to Kindle can deliver. It never carries the relay's host or
credentials.

sender_address.description:
The address books are sent from, which readers must add to their approved
senders at Amazon. Null when no SMTP relay is set up, so nothing can be sent.

KindleSendQueued.description: A Send to Kindle that is queued to go out.

task_id.description: Pass this to `GET /api/kindle/send/status` to follow the send.

KindleSendRequest.description: The book to email to your Kindle address.

book_uuid.description: The book's uuid, at most 64 bytes.

file_id.description:
The `id` of one of the book's files, for a book with several. Leave it out to
send the book's EPUB, or its PDF when it has no EPUB.

KindleSendStatus.description:
Where a Send to Kindle stands. `GET /api/kindle/send/status` returns it for the
`task_id` that `POST /api/kindle/send` gave back. Poll until `status` is no longer
`pending`. A `failed` status carries a `message` that says why.

KoboDeviceView.description:
A Kobo or KOReader registered to your account. Its `token` is the secret that
authenticates the device; for a Kobo it is the sync address's path segment,
`/kobo/{token}/…`.

created_at.description: When it was registered, in Unix seconds.

id.description: The device's id, which the regenerate and delete routes take.

kind.description: Which kind of reader this is.

last_seen_at.description: When the device last synced, in Unix seconds.

last_sync_at.description:
When a KOReader last reported finishing a sync, in Unix seconds. `null` for a Kobo
and for a KOReader that has not synced yet.

last_sync_error.description: What went wrong in a KOReader's last reported sync. `null` when it succeeded.

token.description: The device's secret. Treat it like a password: anyone holding it can sync as you.

KosyncPassword.description: A freshly generated progress-sync password, shown once.

password.description: The new password. It replaces any earlier one, which stops working at once.

username.description: The username to enter in KOReader's Progress sync login.

KosyncStatus.description: Whether you have generated a KOReader progress-sync password.

configured.description: `true` once a password exists; it is not retrievable, only replaceable.

LengthBucket.description:
One step of the book-length spread: a page range and how many books finished in the
period fall in it.

label.description:
The page range, labelled by the server. The `Unknown` bucket holds books whose
length can't be measured, such as audiobooks. Show it too, or the spread covers
fewer books than were finished.

LibraryComposition.description:
What the library is made of: its formats, languages, publishers, publication decades
and genres, as `GET /api/library-composition` returns it. It covers the whole library,
so it is the same for every user. Every count is of books, not files.

books.description:
Books with at least one file. Each dimension's coverage is out of this number. It is
the same count as `books` in `LibrarySize`.

decades.description:
Books by decade of publication, oldest first, with nothing folded. The year is read
the way smart shelf rules read it, so a decade bucket and a `year >= 1990` shelf
agree. There is no unknown bucket. A book with no readable publication date is left
out, and `coverage` shows how many are left out.

formats.description:
Books by file format, most first. A book in two formats counts once in each, so the
buckets add up to `formats.coverage.total`, which is more than `books` by the number
of books held in two formats.

genres.description:
Books by genre, with the smallest folded into "Other". Read its coverage first.
Genres come only from metadata someone edited by hand, so this describes only those
books, not the whole library.

ghosted_books.description:
Books whose files are all gone. They have no format, so no format bucket holds them.
`books` plus `ghosted_books` is every book the library knows of.

languages.description:
Books by language, with the smallest folded into "Other". A book whose file declares
no language is left out rather than counted as unknown.

publishers.description: Books by publisher, with the smallest folded into "Other".

LibraryContents.description: How many ebook and audiobook files the library folders hold, from `GET /api/library`.

LibrarySection.description: The files in one library folder, ebook or audiobook, counted by extension.

counts_by_ext.description:
One `[extension, count]` pair per file extension Omnibus reads, in a fixed order,
zeros included. Empty when no folder is set.

error.description: Why the folder couldn't be read. Null when it was read.

path.description: The configured folder. Null when none is set.

LibrarySize.description:
How big the library is in words, pages and seconds of audio, as
`GET /api/library-size` returns it. It covers the whole library, so it is the same for
every user.

books.description:
Books with at least one file. Each figure's `books` is out of this number. Books
whose files are all gone count nowhere, since nothing can measure them.

listening_seconds.description:
Total seconds of audio. Each audiobook counts once, in the audio format the server
plays, over all its files in that format. A book with any file of unknown length is
left out rather than partly counted.

pages.description:
Total pages. A book's length in pages is its print page count when known, else a
comic's page images, else its word count divided by 275.

words.description: Total words, over the books whose word count is known.

LogPage.description: One page of matching log records, newest first.

has_more.description: Whether more matching records follow this page.

page.description: The zero-based page index that was read.

per_page.description: The page size that was used, after the default and the cap.

records.description: Matching records for this page, newest first.

LogRecord.description: One parsed structured-log record surfaced to the admin log viewer.

fields.description:
The event's other fields and its request's method and path, as compact JSON.
Absent when there was nothing beyond the message.

message.description: The event's `message` field, or empty when the event carried none.

target.description: The module that logged the event, which the `module` filter matches against.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp as logged. Fixed-width, so sorting the strings sorts by time.

client_kind.description:
The kind of client signing in. `ios`, `android` or `bearer` gets a bearer token in
the response body instead of a session cookie. Sent with `device_name`, it also
registers the device.

LoginResponse.description:
The signed-in user, from `POST /api/auth/login` or `POST /api/auth/register`. `token`
is present only for a bearer session. A cookie session comes in the `Set-Cookie`
header instead.

ManifestPart.description: One part of an audiobook file in a `direct` manifest.

MappingConfidence.description: How a position was mapped from one format to the other, from least to most precise.

MatchMode.description:
How a smart shelf combines its conditions. `any` matches a book that meets at least
one. `all` matches a book that meets every one.

McpStatus.description:
Whether the server's hosted MCP endpoint at `/mcp` is on. `GET /api/settings/mcp`
returns it and `POST /api/settings/mcp` takes it.

MeasuredTotal.description:
A library-wide total and how many books it was measured over. Read the two together,
since a total over part of the library is not the size of the whole. Zero `books` means
nothing has been measured yet.

books.description: How many books `total` covers. Never more than the library's book count.

MergeBooksRequest.description:
The two books `POST /api/books/merge` merges. The source book folds into the target
and disappears.

MergeBooksResult.description:
The result of a merge: the id that undoes it, and the uuid of the book that remains.
Pass `merge_log_id` to `POST /api/books/merge/undo` to reverse the merge.

MetadataOverrides.description:
Edits to a book's metadata, laid over what Omnibus read from its file. A field that
is present replaces the file's value, and a list replaces the whole list. Text limits
in characters: 500 for `title`, 50,000 for `description`, and 250 for the other text
fields and for each creator's `name`, `role` and `file_as`.

creators.description: Replaces the whole list of creators. Up to 32.

genres.description:
Replaces the whole list of genres. Up to 64 genres of up to 128 characters each.
Book files carry no genre, so this is where a book's genres come from.

isbn10.description:
An ISBN-10 of 9 digits followed by a digit or `X`, with no hyphens or spaces. An
empty string clears the book's ISBN-10.

isbn13.description:
An ISBN-13 of exactly 13 digits, with no hyphens or spaces. An empty string clears
the book's ISBN-13.

print_pages.description:
The page count of a print edition, from 1 to 20,000. It is not `page_count` on
`EbookMetadata`, which counts the images in a CBZ comic.

series.description: The series name. An empty string takes the book out of its series.

subjects.description: Replaces the whole list of tags. Up to 64 tags of up to 128 characters each.

MetadataSource.description:
A source of book metadata, as a library's precedence list orders them. Only
`embedded_tags`, the metadata inside the book file, and `omnibus_overrides`, the
edits made in Omnibus, supply data today. The others are stored but change nothing.

MonthCount.description: How many books were finished in one calendar month.

month.description: The month, as `YYYY-MM` in your time zone.

PagesReadDetail.description:
What `pages_read` could and couldn't measure in the period. It tells three empty
states apart: no activity, listening only, where zero pages is correct, and reading in
books of unknown length.

audio_books.description:
Books listened to in the period. Audiobooks add no pages, so this tells a
listening-only period apart from an empty one.

daily.description:
Pages read per day in the period, in your time zone, active days only, oldest
first.

measured_books.description: Books whose page progress in the period was measured.

since_day.description:
The day the server began recording page progress, as `YYYY-MM-DD` in UTC. Reading
before it can't be measured.

unmeasured_books.description: Books read in the period whose length is unknown, so the total can't include them.

window_predates_ledger.description:
Whether the period starts before `since_day`, so part of it can't be measured. Use
this rather than working it out from `range`, since only the server knows where the
period starts.

PaletteAuthorHit.description: Author hit for the search palette.

book_count.description: How many books by the author the library holds.

lead_book_title.description:
The title of the author's first book in sort order. Absent when none of the
author's books has a title.

PaletteBookHit.description: A book that matches a palette search, with only what a result row shows.

author_display.description:
The authors' names joined into one string, such as
`Grace Hopper, Margaret Hamilton`.

has_physical.description:
Whether a physical copy is checked in. A book with only a paper copy has an
empty `formats`.

uuid.description: The book's uuid, for routes such as `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}`.

year.description: The four-digit year the book was published. Null when unknown.

PaletteGenreHit.description:
A genre that matches a palette search. A genre has no page of its own, so it carries
no `id`. Search for `genre:<name>` to find its books.

book_count.description: How many books carry the genre.

name.description: The genre's name in one spelling, so `sci-fi` and `Sci-Fi` come back as one hit.

PaletteResults.description:
The matches `GET /api/search/palette` found, grouped by kind. Each list holds up to
5 hits, or up to the request's `limit`. A hit carries only what a result row shows.

author_total.description: How many authors match in all.

book_total.description: How many books match in all, before the list was cut.

duration_ms.description: How long the search took on the server, in milliseconds.

genre_total.description: How many genres match in all.

series_total.description: How many series match in all.

tag_total.description: How many tags match in all.

PaletteSeriesHit.description: Series hit for the search palette.

author_display.description: The first author of the series' first book. Null when it has none.

lead_book_title.description:
The title of the series' first book in sort order. Absent when none of the
series' books has a title.

PaletteTagHit.description: Tag hit for the search palette.

book_count.description: How many books carry the tag.

PeriodComparison.description:
The same figures for the matching stretch of the previous period. The current period
runs to now, so this month so far compares with the same days at the start of last
month, not with all of it. For `all_time`, every figure is zero and `avg_stars` is
null.

pages_read.description:
Pages read in that stretch. It counts whole days in your time zone, so it includes
all of the stretch's last day.

PhysicalCopy.description:
A physical copy of a book. Every user can see it, but only the reader who checked it
in, or an admin, can change its note or remove it. A book can have many copies.

added_by_name.description:
That user's display name, or their username when they have none. Absent once the
account is deleted.

added_by_user_id.description: The id of the user who checked the copy in. Null once that account is deleted.

checked_in_at_iso.description:
When the copy was checked in, as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. It is the same moment
as `checked_in_at`.

isbn.description: The ISBN scanned for this copy. Null when the copy was added without one.

note.description: A free-text note about the copy, such as its edition or publisher.

PositionConfidence.description: How far a client can trust the chapter a `ResolvedPosition` names.

ProgressFormat.description:
Which kind of position a progress record holds. `epub` is a reading position in any
ebook, comics and PDFs included. `audio` is a listening position in an audiobook.

ProgressRecord.description:
Your position in one format of a book, as the server stores it. Only the position
fields of `format` are set.

audio_position_seconds.description:
The listening position of an `audio` record, in seconds from the start of the audio
file. Null for `epub`.

book_file_id.description:
The file the position was taken in. On `GET /api/progress/{uuid}` and
`GET /api/progress/recent`, an `audio` record names the file the position plays in:
the file it was taken in, or the book's first audio file when that one is gone. It
is null there when the book has no audio file left.

client_updated_at.description:
When the device recorded the position, in Unix seconds. The newest one wins. The
server uses its own clock when the update carried no time, and moves a time ahead of
its clock back to it.

derived_epub_cfi.description:
A point CFI for an `epub` record that holds a percent but no CFI, such as one a Kobo
wrote. A reader can open the book there instead of at the start. It never points
past the stored percent. Only `GET /api/progress/{uuid}` fills it. Absent when
`epub_cfi` is set or the server doesn't know the book's structure.

epub_cfi.description:
The reading position of an `epub` record, in the forms `ProgressUpdate` takes. Null
for `audio`, and for an `epub` record that holds only a percent.

kobo_location.description: A Kobo e-reader's own location object, as a JSON string. Only the Kobo sync reads it.

progress_percent.description:
How far through the whole book, from 0 to 100. On `GET /api/progress/{uuid}` and
`GET /api/progress/recent`, an `audio` record carries one computed from its
position. When an `epub` position arrives with only a CFI, the server works out the
percent shortly after, so it can be null for a moment.

oneOf.description:
Where the position is in the book's chapters. Absent when the server can't place
it, and from the `POST /api/progress` response.

total_duration_seconds.description:
The length of the whole audiobook in seconds, across all its files. Absent for
`epub` records. Only `GET /api/progress/{uuid}` and `GET /api/progress/recent` fill
it, so the `POST /api/progress` response leaves it out.

updated_at.description: When the server received the position, in Unix seconds.

bake_errors.description:
The uuids of books whose EPUB couldn't be rebuilt with their edited metadata,
after a rebuild of every EPUB. Absent otherwise, and never present together
with `ghost_warning`.

oneOf.description:
Present when a scan found many books' files missing, though not so many that
it stopped. Clients warn about it.

ProgressState.description:
Where a background task stands. `state` says which case it is. A `running` task
without `total` hasn't counted its work yet. With `total`, `processed` out of `total`
is its progress. `done` and `failed` tasks stay in `recent_complete` for about 10
seconds.

ProgressUpdate.description:
A reading or listening position, as `POST /api/progress` takes it. `format` decides
which position fields apply.

audio_position_seconds.description:
The listening position, in seconds from the start of the audio file. Required for
`audio`, and must be absent for `epub`.

book_file_id.description:
The file the position was taken in, for a book with more than one file of the
format, such as two narrations of one audiobook. It is the `book_file_id` that
`GET /api/audiobooks/{uuid}/manifest` returns. Left out, the server uses the file the
manifest serves by default.

client_updated_at.description:
When the device recorded this position, in Unix seconds. The server keeps the
position with the newest such time, not the one that arrived last. Left out, the
server uses the time the update arrives.

epub_cfi.description:
The reading position, up to 4,096 characters. It is an EPUB CFI, or `comic-page:N` in
a comic and `pdf-page:N` in a PDF, where N is the 0-based page. An `epub` update
needs this or `progress_percent`. Must be absent for `audio`.

kobo_location.description:
A Kobo e-reader's own location object, as a JSON string. The Kobo sync stores it so
the Kobo can resume at the exact spot. Other clients leave it out. Must be absent for
`audio`.

progress_percent.description:
How far through the whole book, from 0 to 100. Unlike a CFI, it means the same thing
on every device. A Kobo sends only this, so for `epub` it can stand in for
`epub_cfi`. Must be absent for `audio`.

ProviderCapabilities.description:
What a provider can be searched by and what it can return, whether or not it is
configured on this server. Each flag describes the provider's API, not any one book.

ProviderEdition.description:
One edition that one provider returned for an edition search. Results from different
providers are never merged, so the same ISBN from two providers comes back as two
entries.

first_publish_year.description:
The year the work was first published, in any edition. `year` is this edition's
own date.

genres.description:
The genres this provider gives the book, at most 10. An empty list means the
provider has none for this book. `carries_genres` in `ProviderCapabilities` says
whether a provider gives genres at all.

isbn10.description:
The ISBN-10 of the same printing as `isbn13`. Present only when the provider
shows that the two name one edition. A 979-prefixed ISBN-13 has no ISBN-10.

isbn13.description:
The ISBN-13 of this edition, as 13 digits with no hyphens. Absent when the
provider ties none to this edition, which is common because a search result
often names a work rather than one printing.

pages.description:
The printed page count of this edition, the value the `print_pages` override
takes. It is never a comic's image count. Null when the provider doesn't say,
and a provider's 0 for unknown also becomes null.

provider_ref.description:
An opaque handle for fetching this edition in full with
`POST /api/metadata/editions/hydrate`, since a search result carries less than
the provider's full record. Send it back unchanged.

relevance.description:
How closely this edition matches the query, in hundredths of a point, where 1000
is a perfect title match. Absent when the result wasn't scored. The score depends
only on the edition and the query, never on the provider, so scores compare
across providers.

series_index.description:
The book's position in `series`, formatted for display, such as "1" or "2.5".
Absent when the provider doesn't say. Only Hardcover gives a position.

year.description: The publication year or date, as free text in the provider's own form.

ProviderInfo.description:
One metadata provider, as `GET /api/metadata/providers` lists it. It never carries an
API key.

configured.description:
Whether the server asks this provider right now. Always true for a provider that
works without a key. A provider that needs a key counts only once one is set.

requires_key.description:
Whether the provider needs an API key at all. A provider whose key is optional
answers without one.

ProviderSearchSource.description: What one provider, named, did for an edition search.

oneOf.description:
The provider answered. `count` is how many of its results are in the returned
list, after the server's cap.
The provider needs an API key this server doesn't have. The server didn't ask it.
The server asked, but no answer came back. `message` says what failed.

The provider limited the server's request rate recently, so the server didn't ask
it this time. `retry_after_secs` says when to try again.

retry_after_secs.description: Whole seconds left on the cooldown, rounded up.

ProviderSearchStatus.description:
What one provider did for an edition search. `kind` tells apart a provider that had
nothing, one the server didn't ask, and one that didn't answer, so an outage never
looks like an empty result.

RankedEntity.description: An author or tag, with the seconds spent in its books during the period.

RatingBucket.description: One step of the rating spread: a rating and how many books were given it in the period.

half_stars.description: The rating in half stars, from 1 to 10. Divide by 2 for stars, so 10 is 5 stars.

RatingRecord.description: Your rating of a book, as the server stores it.

stars.description: The star rating, from 0.5 to 5 in half-star steps.

updated_at.description: When the rating was last set, in Unix seconds.

RatingUpdate.description:
The rating `POST /api/ratings` sets for you on a book. It replaces any rating you gave
the book before.

stars.description: The star rating, from 0.5 to 5 in half-star steps.

ReadStatus.description: Where one user is with a book: not started, reading, or finished.

ReadStatusRecord.description: Your read status for a book, as the server stores it.

finished_at.description:
When the book became finished, in Unix seconds. Setting `finished` on a book that is
already finished keeps the original time. Absent unless `status` is `finished`.

updated_at.description: When the status last changed, in Unix seconds.

updated_at_iso.description: The same moment as `updated_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

ReadingGoal.description: A reader's goal of books to finish in one calendar year, with progress toward it.

current.description:
Books finished in `year`, counted like every other finished-book figure. It can be
more than `target`.

target.description: The number to reach. At least 1. A cleared goal is null, never a zero target.

year.description: The calendar year the goal is for.

ReadingGoalUpdate.description:
The yearly goal `PUT /api/stats/goal` sets or clears. The usual body is
`{"target": 24}`. There is no DELETE route. Send no `target` to clear the goal.

kind.description: What the goal counts. Only `books`, the default.

target.description:
How many books to finish, from 1 to 10,000. Null or absent clears the goal for
`year`.

year.description: The goal's year, from 1900 to 2999. Defaults to this year.

RegisterRequest.description:
A new account for `POST /api/auth/register`, with the same client fields as
`LoginRequest`.

RegistrationStatus.description:
Whether new users can create their own accounts with `POST /api/auth/register`.
`GET /api/auth/registration` returns it and `POST /api/settings/registration` takes it.

RenameApiTokenRequest.description: A new name for an API token, 1 to 100 characters.

ResolveMetaRequest.description:
A title-search result to match against the library. The server matches it as it
would an ISBN, without asking the providers again.

ResolveRequest.description:
An ISBN to look up, scanned or typed. It may be an ISBN-10 or ISBN-13, with or
without hyphens, up to 32 characters.

ResolvedPosition.description:
Where a stored position is in the book: its chapter, and how far through the chapter
and the book. The server works it out from the chapters `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters`
lists, or from the audiobook's chapter marks. Each field but `confidence` is absent
when the book lacks the structure it needs, such as an EPUB with no table of contents.

chapter_ordinal.description:
The chapter's number, counting from 1, so it reads directly against
`chapters_total`.

percent_through_book.description:
How far through the whole book, from 0 to 100, on the same scale as
`progress_percent` in `ProgressRecord`.

percent_through_chapter.description:
How far through the chapter, from 0 to 100. For an ebook, only
`GET /api/progress/{uuid}` fills it.

spine_index.description:
The 0-based index of the spine document, as `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}/chapters` numbers
them. In a PDF it is the page. Absent for audio positions and comic pages.

ResumePoint.description: A book to pick up where you left off, as `GET /api/progress/recent` returns it.

audio_part.description:
The 1-based part of the audiobook the saved position is in, from the audio file's
own marks. Absent for `epub` records. A part is not a book chapter: a 65-chapter
novel stored as a 4-part M4B has four parts. Book chapters are in `record.resolved`.

audio_part_count.description: How many parts the audiobook has. Absent for `epub` records.

oneOf.description:
Where to resume in the other format, for a linked book. Absent when the other
format's position is newer or the position can't be mapped.

linked.description:
Whether you have linked this book's ebook and audiobook. A linked book appears once,
for the format you used last.

playback_rate.description:
Your saved playback speed for this book, such as 1.5. Absent for `epub` records and
when you haven't saved one, which means 1x.

Review.description: Your review of a book, private notes included.

body_html.description: `body_md` rendered to HTML, with unsafe markup removed.

body_md.description: Your public review text, as Markdown. Null when you wrote none.

created_at.description:
When the review first had stars or text, in Unix seconds. Adding text to a review that
had none restarts it, so a text review dates from its text. For a review holding only
notes, when you wrote them.

created_at_iso.description: The same moment as `created_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

notes_html.description: `notes_md` rendered to HTML, with unsafe markup removed.

notes_md.description: Your private notes, as Markdown. Only you ever see them. Null when you wrote none.

rated_at.description: When you last changed the stars, in Unix seconds. Null when there are none.

rated_at_iso.description: The same moment as `rated_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

spoiler.description: Whether you marked the review as containing spoilers.

stars.description: Your star rating, from 0.5 to 5 in half-star steps. Null when you gave none.

updated_at.description:
When you last changed the stars, text or spoiler flag, in Unix seconds. Editing
your notes doesn't move it, because other readers see it too.

updated_at_iso.description: The same moment as `updated_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

ReviewBucket.description: How many readers gave a book one star value.

half_stars.description: The rating in half stars, from 1 to 10. Divide by 2 for stars, so 10 is 5 stars.

ReviewPatch.description:
The changes `PATCH /api/reviews/{uuid}` makes to your review of a book. A field left
out stays as it is; `stars`, `body_md` or `notes_md` sent as null is cleared. Blank
text counts as null. A review left with no stars, text or notes is deleted.

body_md.description: The public review text, as Markdown, up to 65,536 bytes.

notes_md.description: Private notes only you see, as Markdown, up to 65,536 bytes.

spoiler.description:
Whether the review contains spoilers: true or false. Leave it out to keep it; a null
counts as leaving it out and doesn't clear the flag.

stars.description:
The star rating, from 0.5 to 5 in half-star steps. Null clears the stars and keeps
any text and notes.

ReviewSummary.description: Every reader's rating of a book, yours included, summed up.

buckets.description: All ten half-star values, lowest first, zeros included.

ratings.description: How many readers rated the book.

RuleField.description: A field a smart shelf condition can match on.

RuleOp.description: A comparison operator for a smart shelf condition.

RulePreview.description:
How many books a set of conditions matches, out of the `total` in the library, with
up to 12 of the matches as a sample.

RulePreviewRequest.description:
Conditions to try with `POST /api/shelves/preview` without saving a shelf, at most
50.

ScanBook.description: A library book that an ISBN lookup matched, with enough detail to show it.

has_files.description:
Whether the book has a digital file. False for a book that exists only as a
physical copy or a wishlist entry.

has_physical.description: Whether someone has checked in at least one physical copy of the book.

isbn.description:
The book's own ISBN, without separators. In a `close_match` it can differ from
the scanned ISBN. Absent when the book has none.

oneOf.description: The ISBN matches a library book that already has a physical copy.

The ISBN matches a book on the caller's physical wishlist that has no physical
copy yet. Checking the copy in clears the wishlist entry.
The ISBN matches a book the library has digitally, with no physical copy yet.

The providers know the ISBN, and at least one library book has the same title
and author. The reader confirms which one, if any, before anything is written.
Show `book` first, then `others`, as one list to pick from.
The providers know the ISBN, but the library has no such book.
Neither the library nor any provider knows the ISBN.

ScanOutcome.description:
What an ISBN, or a picked title-search result, matched, and so what a client can
offer next. `kind` says which case it is. A `close_match` is never acted on by
itself. The reader confirms it before anything is written.

ScanSearchRequest.description:
Free text to search the metadata providers for, up to 200 characters. It is the
fallback when an ISBN lookup comes back `unresolved`.

ScanSearchResponse.description:
The provider results for a title search. Pass the one the reader picks to
`POST /api/scan/resolve-meta`.

ScanTallies.description:
File counts from a library scan. `found` is how many files it found on disk, and the
other counts say how it sorted them against the index. The counts are final once the
scan has compared every file.

SeriesDetail.description: A series and its books, ordered by `series_index`, from `GET /api/series/{id}`.

reading.description:
Your state on each of `books` that you have opened or marked. A book missing
here is unread, with no position.

SeriesReading.description: Your progress through one series, from `GET /api/series/reading`.

finished.description: How many of the series' books you have finished.

last_read_at.description:
The latest `last_read_at` of your `BookReading` across the series' books, in
Unix seconds.

reading.description: How many of the series' books you are reading now.

SeriesStack.description: A series folded into one row of a book list.

lead_uuid.description: The uuid of the member that stands in the list. The stack takes that book's place.

members.description: Every book of the series that passes the request's filters, in series order.

series_id.description: The series' id, as in `GET /api/series/{id}`. Null when no series record matches.

states.description: Your reading state on each member.

SeriesSummary.description: One series in `GET /api/series`, with its main author.

accent.description: The `accent` of the series' first book that has one.

primary_author.description:
The first creator of the series' first book. Absent when no book in the series
has a linked author.

SessionFormat.description:
Whether a sitting was reading, listening, or both. `mixed` is a book read and listened
to in one stretch.

SessionLogEntry.description:
One sitting in the session log. A sitting is recorded time on one book with no break
over 15 minutes. Sittings under a minute are left out.

ended_at.description: When the sitting ended, in Unix seconds.

ended_at_iso.description: The same moment as `ended_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

seconds.description:
Seconds recorded in the sitting. A sitting with pauses records less than
`ended_at` minus `started_at`.

started_at.description: When the sitting began, in Unix seconds.

started_at_iso.description: The same moment as `started_at`, as an ISO 8601 string in UTC.

SessionLogPage.description: One page of the session log, newest first, as `GET /api/stats/sessions` returns it.

next_before.description:
The `before` value for the next page. Null at the end of the log. Send it back
unchanged, without parsing it.

SessionReport.description:
One stretch of reading or listening, from opening a book to closing it.
`POST /api/progress/sessions` takes up to 500 of them at a time.

client_id.description:
An id the device makes up for the session, such as a UUID, up to 64 characters. A
session whose `client_id` is already stored isn't stored again, so a client can
resend a batch whose response it lost. Without one, a resent session is stored
twice.

ended_at.description: When the session ended, in Unix seconds. Must not be before `started_at`.

progress_units.description: Seconds spent reading or listening in the session. Must not be negative.

started_at.description: When the session started, in Unix seconds.

time_zone.description:
The device's IANA time zone when the session was recorded, such as
`America/Los_Angeles`, up to 64 characters. It goes with `utc_offset_minutes`. The
offset says what the clock read, and the zone says where. An offset of `-420` is Los
Angeles in summer and Phoenix all year. The server stores the name without checking
it.

utc_offset_minutes.description:
The device's offset from UTC in minutes when the session was recorded, east
positive: `-420` for UTC-7, `330` for UTC+05:30. From -720 to 840. The time-of-day
and weekday stats place the session by it, and leave out a session without one.

SessionView.description:
A signed-in session, as its owner or an admin sees it. It carries enough to name and
end the session, never its token. `GET /api/auth/sessions` and
`GET /api/admin/users/{id}/sessions` return it.

client.description:
A readable name for the client that holds the session. It is the device name a
native client registered, such as "Seamus's iPhone", or a label built from the
browser's `User-Agent`, such as "Firefox on macOS". It is "Unknown client" when
neither is known.

is_current.description:
True for the session this request signed in with. Only `GET /api/auth/sessions`
sets it. The admin listing always returns false, even for the admin's own
session. `DELETE /api/auth/sessions/{id}` refuses to end the current session
with a 400.

kind.description: `cookie` for a browser session, `bearer` for a token session.

recorded.description:
How many sessions named a book the server knows; it drops the rest, so this can be
less than the number sent. A session repeating a stored `client_id` counts here but
isn't stored twice.

SetBookDetailScrollStops.description: Whether a book's detail page stops at each section as you scroll.

enabled.description: `true` stops at each section; `false` scrolls the page in one piece.

SetFollowMode.description: Whether `POST /api/books/{uuid}/cross-format-follow` turns follow mode on or off.

SetGoogleBooksKey.description: A Google Books API key to save, or none to clear the saved one.

key.description:
The Google Books API key, up to 512 bytes. Null, left out or blank clears the
saved key.

SetHardcoverKey.description: A Hardcover API key to save, or none to clear the saved one.

key.description:
The Hardcover API token, up to 2048 bytes. Null, left out or blank clears the
saved key.

SetHiddenFormats.description: The formats to hide from your library view.

formats.description:
Format names such as `cbz`, each 1 to 16 letters or digits, at most 32. Case and
duplicates don't matter. An empty or missing list hides nothing.

email.description:
The address books are emailed to, such as `name@kindle.com`. Null, missing or
blank clears it.

display_name.description:
The name other readers see, up to 64 characters with no control characters.
Null, missing or blank clears it, and your username shows instead.

SetReadStatus.description: The read status `PUT /api/read-status` sets for you on a book.

SetShareStats.description: Whether other readers on this server can see your reading stats.

enabled.description: `true` shares your stats with the household; `false` keeps them to yourself.

SetStackSeries.description: Whether your library grid shows each series as one tile.

enabled.description: `true` folds a series into one tile; `false` shows every book on its own.

Settings.description: The server's library folders, and how often it rescans them.

scan_interval_hours.description:
Hours between automatic rescans of both libraries, at least 1. When absent, the
server rescans only at startup or when `POST /api/scan-library` asks it to.

Shelf.description: A shelf in full, with its description, conditions and match mode.

oneOf.description: How the conditions combine. Set for a smart shelf, null for any other kind.

owner_has_avatar.description: Whether the owner has an avatar at `GET /api/users/{owner_user_id}/avatar`.

owner_username.description: The owner's display name, or their username when they have none.

sync_to_kobo.description:
Whether the owner's sync devices (Kobos and KOReaders) sync this shelf's books. Off
by default. A device syncs only books on shelves with this on, never the whole
library.

ShelfKind.description: The kind of a shelf, fixed when it is created.

ShelfPage.description: A shelf's books, all in one response, up to 50,000.

ShelfRule.description:
One smart shelf condition. What `value` holds, and which `op` values work, depend on
`field`:

- `tag`, `genre`, `author`, `series`: a name, matched ignoring case, with `is`,
  `is_not`, `contains` or `starts_with`.
- `format`: a format name such as `epub`, with `includes`, `contains` or
  `starts_with`.
- `rating`: a star rating from 0.5 to 5, with `is` or `gte`.
- `year`: a year, with `is` or `gte`.
- `status`: `unread`, `reading` or `finished`, with `is`.
- `date_added`, `date_updated`: a window such as `30d`, `2w`, `3m` or `1y` with
  `in_last`, a `START..END` range of `YYYY-MM-DD` dates with `between`, or one
  `YYYY-MM-DD` date with `before` or `after`.

`value` may be up to 512 characters.

ShelfSummary.description:
A shelf in a list of shelves: who owns it, its kind, visibility, accent color and
book count.

cover_uuids.description:
The uuids of up to four of the shelf's books that have covers, in the shelf's
order.

owner_has_avatar.description: Whether the owner has an avatar at `GET /api/users/{owner_user_id}/avatar`.

owner_username.description: The owner's display name, or their username when they have none.

SmtpConfigStatus.description:
The server-wide SMTP relay settings, with the password masked. It never carries the
password itself.

password_masked.description:
A masked preview of the password, such as `hunt…ter2`, or `••••` for a password
of 8 characters or fewer. Null when no password is set.

source.description:
Where the settings in effect come from: `settings` when saved through the API,
`env` when read from the server's environment variables, or `none`.

SmtpConfigUpdate.description:
The server-wide SMTP relay that Send to Kindle emails through. Every field but
`password` replaces the saved value.

password.description:
The relay password, up to 1024 bytes. Null or left out keeps the saved password.
An empty string clears it.

SmtpSecurity.description: How the server secures its connection to the SMTP relay.

SortDir.description: The direction of a `SortKey` order: ascending or descending.

SortKey.description: The order to list books in.

SpoilerFilter.description:
What to do with search hits past your reading position. The default, `annotate`,
marks them, so a caller can say an answer exists but lies ahead. `exclude` is for a
caller that must not see them at all.

StackMemberState.description: Your reading state on one book of a series stack.

percent.description: Your ebook position as a whole-book percent, from 0 to 100. Null without one.

started.description:
Whether you have opened the book in any format, meaning it has a status, a percent
or a listening position.

StatsRange.description:
The period reading stats cover. Each calendar period runs from its start to now, in
your time zone.

StatsSummary.description:
One reader's stats for one period, as `GET /api/stats` returns them. Days are cut on
the request's `utc_offset_minutes`. A book counts as finished when its read status is
set to `finished` or a journal entry on it says 100 percent. It counts once if both
happen, and only while the book is still in the library. Every finished-book figure
uses this rule. `pages_read` measures ground covered instead.

active_days.description: Days in the period with any reading or listening.

as_of_day.description:
Today, as `YYYY-MM-DD` in your time zone, when the stats were computed. Use it as the
last day of the heatmap instead of the device's clock.

avg_stars.description:
The mean of the ratings given in the period, from 0.5 to 5. Null when nothing was
rated.

books_active.description: Books with any reading or listening in the period.

books_per_month.description:
Books finished in each of the last 12 calendar months, oldest first, ending with the
current month so far. It doesn't depend on `range`.

books_this_year.description:
Books finished in the current calendar year, whether or not a yearly goal is set. It
is the same count as `current` in `goal`, so setting a goal never changes it. It
doesn't depend on `range`.

busiest_week_seconds.description:
Seconds read and listened in the busiest week, counting only its days inside the
period.

busiest_week_start.description:
The Monday that starts the busiest week, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, even when nothing was read
that Monday. It can fall before the period starts. Null when the period has no
activity.

current_streak_days.description:
The run of consecutive active days still going on `as_of_day`. A run that ended
yesterday still counts. One that ended earlier gives zero. Unlike most figures here,
it doesn't depend on `range`.

daily_goals.description:
The reader's daily goals and today's progress toward them. They don't depend on
`range`.

day_of_week.description:
Seconds read and listened in the period by weekday, for all 7, Monday first, zeros
included. It counts the same sessions as `hour_of_day`, so the two add up to the same
total.

finished_books.description:
Books finished in the period, newest first, up to 100. `books_finished` has the full
count.

genre_share.description: Every genre read in the period, not only the largest.

genre_tagged_books.description:
Books with a genre and any activity in the period. `genre_share` counts these books.
Never more than `books_active`. The difference is reading the genres can't describe.

oneOf.description:
The reader's goal for the current calendar year. Null when none is set. It doesn't
depend on `range`.

heatmap.description: Seconds read and listened per day in the period, active days only, oldest first.

hour_of_day.description:
Seconds read and listened in the period by hour of the day, for all 24 hours in
order, zeros included. Each session is placed by the UTC offset it recorded. Sessions
without one aren't counted here, and `unzoned_seconds` reports them instead.

length_buckets.description:
Books finished in the period, by length, plus the `Unknown` bucket. Every bucket is
present, zeros included. All zeros means nothing was finished.

listening_daily.description: Seconds listened per day in the period, active days only, oldest first.

listening_seconds.description: Seconds spent listening in the period.

longest_streak_days.description: The longest run of consecutive active days in the period.

pages_detail.description:
What `pages_read` could and couldn't measure in the period, and the day the server
began recording page progress.

pages_per_hour.description:
Estimated reading speed, in pages per hour. It is a mean over the books finished in
the period that have a known length and recorded reading time, weighted by reading
time. It is not `pages_read` divided by `reading_seconds`, which cover different
books. It counts reading time only, so a book partly listened to looks faster than
it was. Null when no finished book qualifies.

pages_read.description:
Pages read in the period. It is how far each book was carried during it, measured
against the book's length in pages. Exact for some books and an estimate for others.
A book of unknown length adds nothing. Null when no book read in the period has a
known length, so read `pages_detail` before showing that as no data.

previous.description: The same figures for the matching stretch of the previous period.

rating_histogram.description:
How the period's ratings spread across the ten half-star steps. All ten are present,
zeros included. An empty list means no ratings in the period. It counts the same
ratings `avg_stars` averages.

rating_monthly.description:
The mean rating given in each of the last 12 calendar months, oldest first. It
doesn't depend on `range`. A month with no ratings carries 0, which no real mean can
be, so show it as empty rather than as a low rating.

reading_seconds.description: Seconds spent reading in the period.

sessions.description:
Sittings in the period. A sitting is recorded time on one book with no break over 15
minutes. Sittings under a minute don't count here, though their seconds still count
in the totals.

top_authors.description: Up to 8 authors with the most time spent in their books in the period, most first.

top_tags.description: Up to 8 tags with the most time spent in their books in the period, most first.

unzoned_seconds.description:
Seconds in the period from sessions that recorded no UTC offset, such as older ones,
so they can't be placed on a local clock. Above zero, it means `hour_of_day` and
`day_of_week` cover less than the whole period. It is not an error.

StorageStats.description: Disk use, in bytes, of the book library and each cache Omnibus keeps.

library_bytes.description: The total size of every indexed book file. It is not a cache, so it has no cap.

SuggestionCard.description:
One cleanup suggestion with the names and counts to show it for review.
`secondary_name` and `photo_url` are null when they don't apply: a tag split has no
single other name, and only author suggestions can have a photo.

book_count.description: How many library books are affected if the suggestion is applied.

created_at.description: Unix seconds the suggestion was detected.

photo_url.description:
Relative URL of the author's cached photo. Null for other kinds and for an
author without one.

primary_name.description:
The name the suggestion centres on: the record a merge keeps, the tag being
split, the record being deleted, or a book's current title.

proposed_parts.description:
The tags a split would produce, in the order they appear in the original. Empty
for every other action.

secondary_name.description:
The suggestion's second name, where it has one: the proposed title on a rename,
or the record folding away in a two-way merge. Null for a split, a delete, and
a merge of three or more records, which `source_names` lists instead.

source_names.description: Every name a merge would fold into `primary_name`. Empty for the other actions.

oneOf.description: The server has no Hardcover API key, so it can't fetch suggestions.
The server is fetching suggestions and has none cached yet. Ask again later.

The cached suggestions. An empty `items` means Hardcover had nothing usable, and
that answer is cached too.

SuggestionsResponse.description:
A book's Hardcover suggestions, or why there are none yet. `status` says which case
it is.

SummarySource.description: A provider to fetch a book summary from.

Superlatives.description:
The period's records, such as its longest book and its longest sitting. Every field
is optional. A period without enough data for a record leaves it out rather than
naming its only book.

oneOf.description:
The day with the most seconds read and listened in the period. A tie goes to the
earliest day.

The book finished in the period in the fewest days from its first recorded session.
A book read within one day counts as one day. Only books with at least 30 minutes of
recorded time qualify. Reading the server never recorded doesn't count, so the real
time can be longer. Present it as at least that many days.

The longest book finished in the period, in pages. Absent when no book finished in
the period has a known length.
The longest sitting in the period, in seconds of recorded time.

The shortest book finished in the period, in pages. Absent when it would be the same
book as `longest_book`, or have the same page count.

TagWeight.description: A tag and the number of books that carry it.

TaskDetail.description:
Live detail about a task: its phase, the item it is on and, for a scan, its file
counts. Every field may be absent.

current_item.description: The item the task is working on, such as "books/Author/Title.epub".

phase.description: A short label for the task's current phase, such as "Walking the library".

oneOf.description:
A scan's file counts. They stay on the finished task, so a client can sum up what
the scan changed.

TaskKind.description:
The kind of a background task. `scan` also covers the jobs that follow a scan and
other jobs without a kind of their own. More kinds may come, so clients should accept
values they don't know.

TaskProgress.description:
One background task in the progress feed. `task_id` identifies it until the server
restarts.

oneOf.description: Live detail about the task. Absent for kinds of task that don't report it.

last_update_ms.description: When the task last reported progress, in Unix milliseconds.

resource_key.description:
What the task works on, such as a library folder or a book. Tasks with the same
key run one after another. Absent when the task claims nothing.

started_at_ms.description:
When the task started, in Unix milliseconds by the server's clock. It is for
showing elapsed time only.

TrendPoint.description: A day or a month on a trend, and a figure's value over it.

label.description: The day as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or the month as `YYYY-MM`, depending on the trend.

UndoMergeRequest.description:
The merge `POST /api/books/merge/undo` reverses, by the `merge_log_id` the merge
returned.

UndoMergeResult.description: The uuid of the source book that undoing a merge restored.

UpdateBookmark.description: The new name or note `PUT /api/bookmarks/{id}` gives a bookmark.

title.description: The bookmark's name or note, up to 512 characters. Null or absent clears it.

UpdateCopyNoteRequest.description:
A new note for a physical copy, up to 4096 characters. Null, left out or blank clears
the note.

UpdateHighlightNote.description: The note `PATCH /api/highlights/{id}/note` puts on a highlight.

note.description: The note, up to 4,096 characters. Null or absent removes the note.

UpdateJournalEntry.description: The new content `PATCH /api/journals/{id}` gives one of your journal entries.

body_md.description: The entry's new Markdown source. It must not be blank, and can be up to 65,536 bytes.

progress.description: How far through the book you are, from 0 to 100. Null clears it.

oneOf.description:
The entry's new status, such as `published` to publish a draft. Null or absent keeps
the current status.

UpdateShelfRequest.description:
Changes to a shelf. A field left out or null stays as it is. `rules` replaces every
condition, and applies to smart shelves only.

sync_to_kobo.description: Turns device sync for the shelf on or off.

UploadCommitResult.description: The uuid of the book an upload created. `GET /api/ebooks/{uuid}` reads it.

UploadInspection.description:
The metadata `POST /api/uploads/ebooks/inspect` reads from an uploaded file, as the
library would index it. Correct it and send it with `POST /api/uploads/ebooks`, where
`title` and `author` name the folder the file is saved in.

author.description: The first creator the file declares.

cover_preview.description:
A small `data:` URL of the file's cover, to show before the book exists. Null
when the file has no cover or it can't be decoded.

creators.description: Every creator the file declares, in file order, starting with `author`.

ext.description: The file's format as a lowercase extension, such as `epub`.

has_cover.description: Whether the file carries a cover.

isbn13.description: The ISBN-13 found among the file's identifiers, as `isbn13` on `EbookMetadata`.

subjects.description: The file's subjects, which become the book's tags.

UserPermissions.description:
The four permission flags that say what a user may do. The server stores each flag
separately. Most checks let an admin through, but a few read the flag itself, such as
`can_download` for downloads.

UserSummary.description:
A user account: who it is, what it may do, and its saved preferences. It never
carries a password.

book_detail_scroll_stops.description:
Whether a book's detail page stops at each section as the user scrolls. False,
the default, scrolls the page in one piece.

display_name.description:
The name other users see. When null, clients show `username`, which stays the
sign-in name.

has_avatar.description:
Whether the user has uploaded an avatar. When true, `GET /api/users/{id}/avatar`
serves it. When false, clients show a monogram.

hidden_formats.description:
The formats the user hides from their library view, as lowercase names such as
`cbz`. Pass them as `exclude_formats` on `GET /api/ebooks`. An empty list hides
nothing.

kindle_email.description: The address Send to Kindle emails books to. Null when the user hasn't set one.

share_stats.description:
Whether other readers on this server may see the user's reading stats. True by
default.

stack_series.description: Whether the user's library grid shows each series as one tile.

Visibility.description: Who can see a shelf. `private` means its owner and admins. `public` means every user.

WeekdayBucket.description: One day of the week and the seconds read and listened on it during the period.

label.description: The weekday's short name, such as `Mon`.

weekday.description: The weekday where each session happened, from 0 for Monday to 6 for Sunday.

WishlistAddRequest.description:
A book to add to the caller's physical wishlist. Set `book_uuid` for a library book,
or `meta` to create a new book with no files. When both are set, the server uses
`book_uuid` and ignores `meta`.

WishlistEntry.description:
A book on one user's physical wishlist. Each book is on a user's wishlist at most
once.

WishlistRemoval.description:
What removing a wishlist entry did. A book with no file, no physical copy and no
other reader's wish goes with its last wishlist entry. `book_deleted` is then true,
and the book no longer exists.

WishlistSource.description: Where a wishlist entry was added from.

WorkerQueueEntry.description:
One kind of background task: how many are queued or running, and how long recent ones
took.

recent_completions_ms.description:
How long each of the last 20 finished tasks took, in milliseconds, oldest first.
Failed tasks count too.

WorkerStatus.description:
The background task progress feed: tasks running now, and tasks that finished in the
last 10 seconds or so. Both lists are sorted by `task_id`.

bearer.description: A session token from `POST /api/auth/login`, or an API token (`omni_…`) from `POST /api/auth/api-tokens`.

media_token.name: token
media_token.description: A bearer token passed in the URL, for media that an `` or `

session_cookie.name: __Host-omnibus_session
session_cookie.description: The cookie a browser sign-in sets. A server running without secure cookies (`OMNIBUS_SECURE_COOKIES=0`) names it `omnibus_session` instead.
